id: AJC.picrep.divzero
title: 'Div-zero: the first DivFamily producer, and Div^0 representable by the terminal
  object'
projects:
- Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge
summary: 'ADVANCED, NOT CLOSED. Commits 0d465e95d9, aa38db9d26, and 10d411758b add
  a rooted, axiom-clean terminal-representability bridge and two conditional Div^0
  RepresentableBy constructors. The reduction is honest: DivFunctorDeg pi 0 is represented
  by the terminal object once every degree-zero divisor family has zero structure
  sheaf, equivalently once x.HasFiberDeg 0 implies IsZero x.F. That coherent-sheaf
  vanishing premise is still unproduced, so this is a producer modulo one non-circular
  hypothesis, not an instantiated producer. The PicEt seam and fgaPicardRepresentability
  remain untouched.'

      "body": "**FGA picSharp rewire LANDED (run 0008): route-(b) conventions + two standing caveats.**\n\nState after the rewire (`Picard/FGAPicRepresentability.lean`, **4 real `sorry`s**, all TRUE statements \u2014 Ground-verified run 0008 reconcile):\n\n- `picSharp C := PicSharp.relPresheaf C \u22d9 forget AddCommGrpCat` (`Type (u+1)`-valued, REAL). `Scheme.HasRationalPoint C` = Nonempty section subtype of `C.hom`; the ONE genuine FGA sorry is `instHasPicScheme [HasRationalPoint C]`. The other three are typed-sorry carriers: `PicSchemeLocallyOfFiniteType` (Kleiman \u00a74 `th:main`(1), true under the rational point) and the pre-existing Quot-blocked `HasDivFunctor` / `HasAbelMap`.\n- `instPicSharpRepresentable` proved by `choose_spec`; `groupSchemeStructure : CommGrpObj (PicScheme C)` proved via `CommGrpObj.ofRepresentableBy` + a `Multiplicative.ofAdd` NatIso (`picSharpCommGrpForgetIso`, naturality is `rfl` \u2014 no defeq walls anywhere in this file).\n- Consumers: quantify over `[HasPicScheme C]` (synthesized from `[HasRationalPoint C]`) \u2014 `degree`/`kPoints_iff_kerDegree` in `IdentityComponent.lean` now carry it. `Pic0Scheme C := GroupScheme.IdentityComponent (PicScheme C)` is now a real def (axiom-clean), gated on `PicSchemeLocallyOfFiniteType`.\n\n**Caveat 1 \u2014 pointless curves:** `JacobianWitness` (`Jacobian.lean`) requires the abelian variety $J$ to exist UNconditionally, but route (b) only builds `PicScheme` for pointed $C$. For a genus-$\\ge 1$ curve without a rational point the eventual `picardJacobianWitness` proof needs Galois/\u00e9tale descent from a finite extension where $C$ gains a point (or a pointed restatement of the north star). Not blocking anything now \u2014 record before anyone tries to close `picardJacobianWitness` directly.\n\n**Caveat 2 \u2014 `smoothProperQuotient` statement is WEAKER than Kleiman lm:qt and unprovable as stated:** Mathlib v4.31 has NO quasi-projectivity vocabulary, so hypothesis (2) of lm:qt is missing from the Lean statement; without it the statement is FALSE (Hironaka-type free \u2124/2 action on a smooth proper non-projective 3-fold: smooth proper equivalence relation, \u00e9tale-quotient sheaf a non-scheme algebraic space). The former GLOBAL `instHasSmoothProperQuotient \u27e8sorry\u27e9` (every presheaf representable!) was deleted this run (Ground-confirmed gone); the class is a use-site hypothesis only.       "body": "[persistent] [persistent] REPRESENTABILITY PUSH, 2026-07-29 \u2014 the claim/lane protocol that makes 10 free-objective lanes not collide.\n\nWHY THIS EXISTS. This round replaces prescriptive per-leaf tasks with FIVE lanes per project: one REVIEWER and four PROVERS ranked p1..p4. The provers each pick their own target. That only works if claiming is explicit and public. This item is the claiming mechanism. Read it before your first edit.\n\nTHE FIVE LANES PER PROJECT\n- `review-ajc` / `review-ajcr` \u2014 reviewer. Read-mostly. Finds defects of ROUTE and ORGANISATION, not of individual proofs; may propose refactors and file tasks-as-proposals for the provers. Does not race provers for proof work.\n- `ajc-p1` / `ajcr-p1` \u2014 takes the MOST important open representability item.\n- `-p2`, `-p3`, `-p4` \u2014 2nd, 3rd, 4th most important, where \"important\" is measured against the project's representability headline, not by ease.\n\nCLAIMING \u2014 do this BEFORE you start proving, not after.\n 1. `horizon roadmap list --focus <your project's w4-rep / picrep subtree>` and read the reviewer's open notes.\n 2. Pick your item. Check no other lane owns it: an item with `--owner` set to another lane IS CLAIMED. Do not take it, even if you think you would be faster.\n 3. Claim it: `horizon roadmap set <id> --owner <your-task-id> --status active`. If your target is not yet a roadmap item, `roadmap add` it under the right parent first, then claim it.\n 4. Announce: one `horizon inbox add --kind info --to horizon --body \"CLAIM <lane>: <roadmap id> \u2014 <one line on what discharging it buys>\"`.\n 5. Release on exit: if you did NOT finish, `roadmap set <id> --owner ''` and leave a one-line inbox note saying where you stopped and what the next lane should NOT re-derive. An item left owned by a dead lane is worse than an unclaimed one.\n\nRANK IS A TIE-BREAK, NOT A FENCE. If p1's item turns out to be blocked on p3's, say so in the inbox and swap \u2014 rank exists so four lanes do not all converge on the same top item, not to stop you working on the right thing. p1 has first refusal on any contested item.\n\nYOU MAY PROPOSE WORK TO THE OTHER LANES. Direct-message with `horizon inbox add --kind hint --to task:<lane-id> --body \"\u2026\"`. A good proposal names the declaration, the file, and why it is worth more than what that lane currently holds. You may NOT reassign another lane's claimed item, and you may NOT create new horizon runs or tasks for teams outside your own (`horizon permissions` is false on both counts \u2014 propose to the human instead).\n\nSTANDING BINDING DECISIONS you must not relitigate: `I-0491` (AJC: no rational-point binder on the headline; `hasRationalPoint_of_curve` is FALSE and must be deleted, never proved) and `I-0492` (AJCR: `DivFamZar` widens to arbitrary affine opens; do NOT build the GL_2/Aut(P1) route). Read both.\n\nWHAT COUNTS AS PROGRESS, given the 2026-07-29 audit. That audit found 99 of 101 sampled representability claims refuted: 67 sorry-reachable, 17 VACUOUS, 12 hypothesis-shifted. So the bar is explicit:\n- A discharged obligation must be sorry-free AND its hypotheses must be inhabitable. Before you claim a gate closed, exhibit a witness for every antecedent, or say plainly which antecedent is still undischarged.\n- Do NOT add a class, structure field, or hypothesis whose statement does not mention the object it is supposedly about. `HasDivFunctor` is the cautionary case: its field asserted only that a presheaf category is nonempty, `C` did not occur, and it was advertised as the existence of the relative divisor functor. That is a vacuity, and it survived because nobody read the statement.\n- Do NOT discharge an obligation by projecting the hypothesis you assumed (`choose_spec.1` of your own binder). That is `P \u2192 P`.\n- A green `lake build` is not evidence a statement is non-vacuous. Check imports are current before believing a `lean_multi_attempt` success.\n\nCOMMIT DISCIPLINE. This is ONE shared ledger branch with 10 writers. Another lane's integrate sweep can commit your half-written file before you have measured it once. Write risky proofs as explicit `sorry` first, measure, then fill. Stage explicit files, never `add -A`.",

Announce: one `horizon inbox add --kind info --to horizon --body \"CLAIM <lane>: <roadmap id> \u2014 <one line on what discharging it buys>\"`.\n 5.       "summary": "HALF LANDED 2026-07-25 (run 0048, commit on Picard/DivSchemeCertZarChartPair.lean).\n\nWHAT IS DONE. No fibre, no tube, no packet idempotent.\nNone of the landed no-gos touches this configuration: not_exists_unique_support_piece refutes ONE\nsupport-meeting piece and this has TWO; supportLocus_disjoint_chart_inter_of_separated refutes\nseparation and this adaptation is maximally unseparated.\n\nWHAT REMAINS: the CHART-PRINCIPALITY input, i.e. produce the (pt, eqn, unit) datum. It says the\ndivisor is cut by a single equation on each pinned chart. def extract_declarations(text: str, *, library: str, file: str) -> list[Declaration]:
    """Parse one Lean source into declarations. Heuristic, not a real parser."""
    lines = text.splitlines()
    ns: list[str] = []
    pending_doc: str | None = None
    out: list[Declaration] = []
    i = 0
    while i < len(lines):
        stripped = lines[i].strip()
        if not stripped:
            i += 1
            continue

        if stripped.startswith("/--"):
            doc, end = _read_docstring(lines, i)
            pending_doc = doc
            i = end + 1
            continue
        if stripped.startswith("/-"):  # module/section comment — skip the block
            j = i
            while j < len(lines) and "-/" not in lines[j]:
                j += 1
            i = j + 1
            continue

        if stripped.startswith("@["):  # attribute line — keep any pending docstring
            i += 1
            continue

        m_ns = _NAMESPACE_RE.match(stripped)
        if m_ns:
            ns.append(m_ns.group(1))
            pending_doc = None
            i += 1
            continue
        m_end = _END_RE.match(stripped)
        if m_end:
            if ns and (m_end.group(1) is None or ns[-1].endswith(m_end.group(1))):
                ns.pop()
            i += 1
            continue

        m = _DECL_RE.match(stripped)
        if m:
            kind, raw_name = m.group(1), m.group(2).lstrip("@")
            qualified = ".".join([*ns, raw_name]) if raw_name else ".".join(ns)
            out.append(Declaration(
                name=qualified,
                kind=kind,
                signature=_collect_signature(lines, i),
                doc=pending_doc or "",
                library=library,
                file=file,
                line=i + 1,
            ))
            pending_doc = None
            i += 1
            continue

        pending_doc = None
        i += 1
    return out

-import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.DivDegree

-
-/-!
-# The empty divisor: the first inhabitant of `Scheme.DivFamily`
-
-`Scheme.DivFamily π T` (`Picard/DivFunctorDef.lean`) is the carrier of the whole
-divisor side of the Milne–Kollár campaign: `Scheme.DivFunctor`, its degree slices
-`Scheme.DivFunctorDeg`, the Abel maps `abelDeg` / `abelMapWitness`, the flatness
-inputs of `Picard/DivPushforwardFlat.lean`, and `IdentityComponent`'s
-`ClassDegreePinned` acceptance test are all quantified over it. Until this file it
-had **zero producers**, for any `π`, any base, and any test object including the
-trivial one — measured with `exact?` and recorded in its own docstring. The
-consequence recorded there: *every* statement quantified over a `DivFamily` was
-"true but untested", with no instance to be wrong about.
-
-This file supplies the first inhabitant, unconditionally in `π : X ⟶ S` and
-`T : Over S`: the **empty divisor** `D = ∅`, whose structure sheaf `O_D` is the
-zero module and whose ideal is all of `O_{X_T}`.
-
-## Why the empty divisor satisfies the divisor condition
-
-The divisor condition of `DivFamily` is that the kernel ideal `I = ker q` be
-*invertible* (`LineBundle.IsLocallyTrivial`). For `q : O_{X_T} ⟶ 0` the kernel is
-`O_{X_T}` itself (`Limits.kernelZeroIsoSource`), and the structure sheaf is
-trivially locally trivial (`Scheme.PicSharp.isLocallyTrivial_unit`, restated here as
-`isLocallyTrivial_unit'` because that one is `private`). So the invertible-ideal
-condition — the field that makes `DivFamily` a divisor rather than an arbitrary
-quotient — holds *for the reason it should*: `O_{X_T}/O_{X_T} = 0` cuts out the
-empty subscheme, an effective divisor of degree zero.
-
-The three remaining fields are properties of the zero module, and the file proves
-each rather than assuming it:
-
-* `isFinitePresentation` — the zero module is finitely presented. Mathlib has no
-  instance for this (measured: `infer_instance` and `exact?` both fail on
-  `(0 : Y.Modules).IsFinitePresentation`), so §1 builds the `QuasicoherentData`:
-  the singleton family `{⊤}` covers the top of the opens site
-  (`coversTop_singleton_top`), the restriction functor preserves zero objects
-  (`preservesZeroMorphisms_overFunctor`, proved from `PresheafOfModules` extensionality
-  because instance search for it times out), and a zero sheaf of modules has an
-  *empty* presentation — no generators and no relations, both trivially finite.
-* `flat` — flatness over the base. The section modules of a zero module are
-  subsingletons, and a subsingleton module is flat.
-* `properSupport` — the schematic support of the zero module is the subscheme cut
-  out by the annihilator, which is `⊤`, so the support is **empty**
-  (`Scheme.IdealSheafData.instIsEmptyCarrierCarrierCommRingCatSubschemeTop`) and any
-  morphism out of it is proper via `IsProper.instOfIsFinite`. It is free here for that
-  reason, and in particular with **no properness assumption on `π`**. (An earlier
-  revision added "and it is a real hypothesis for a nonempty divisor". That half was
-  never measured — nothing here or elsewhere in the project exhibits a divisor where
-  `properSupport` fails or is expensive, and `DivFunctorDef.lean` says it is *automatic*
-  when `π` is proper. Dropped rather than repaired: the free-here half is what this
-  file establishes.)
-
-## What this does and does not buy
-
-**Does**: the divisor cluster is no longer vacuous. `Nonempty (DivFamily π T)` for
-every `π` and `T`; `(DivFunctor π).obj (op T)` and `(DivFunctorDeg π 0).obj (op T)`
-are inhabited; `HasFiberDeg zero 0`; and the base-change action carries `zero` to
-`zero` (`pullbackAlong_zero`), so the classes are a global section of `DivFunctor`
-rather than a fibrewise accident. Every theorem in `DivDegree.lean` and
-`DivPushforwardFlat.lean` now has a witness to be checked against.
-
-**Does not**: this closes no `sorry` and witnesses no antecedent of
-`Scheme.fgaPicardRepresentability`. In particular it is *not* a step of D1′: the
-campaign's D1′ wants divisor families of a **prescribed positive degree** `d`
-arising from a very ample `O(1)`, which needs the projectivity input
-(`AJC.picrep.projectivity`) and P5 uniform `H¹` vanishing. What the empty divisor
-does for that programme is remove the possibility that the target type is
-uninhabited — a question that had to be settled before any positive-degree producer
-could be believed, and which no lane had settled in either direction.
-
-**One caveat, stated because it is the natural over-reading.** The degree-zero slice
-being inhabited does *not* make `DivFunctorDeg π 0` representable by the terminal
-object `Over.mk (𝟙 S)`. That would need the slice to be a *singleton* at every test
-object, and this file proves only the `Nonempty` half. The missing half is
-`Subsingleton ((DivFunctorDeg π 0).obj (op T))` — i.e. that the empty divisor is the
-*only* relative divisor of degree `0`. That is the expected statement (a degree-`0`
-effective divisor on a fibre of a relative curve is empty), but it is a fact about
-`fiberDeg`, not a formality: `fiberDeg` is a `finrank` with a junk value at
-infinite dimension. Neither direction is proved here.
-
-**Corrected, and the correction is the useful part** (fresh-context audit of this file,
-2026-07-30). An earlier revision of this paragraph said "no lane holds it". That is
-FALSE: the analogous `Subsingleton` *is* landed, hours earlier, on the **sibling**
-project's carrier — `instSubsingletonDivFamZarZero`
-(`AJCR Picard/DivisorFamilyDegreeZeroUnique.lean`) and, over an arbitrary test ring,
-`instSubsingletonDivFamZarZeroGeneral` plus a full `RepresentableBy` producer
-(`AJCR Picard/DivisorFamilyDegreeZeroRep.lean`).
-
-What survives, for a **sharper** reason than the carrier mismatch: their proof is not
-portable because it never passes through a `finrank` at all. It runs on `IsCertified`
-and `rankAtStalk_eq_zero_iff_subsingleton` over `Away` localisations of section rings,
-machinery that exists only on the Zariski-certified carrier `DivFamZar : Type u`. AJC's
-`fiberDeg` is a `Module.finrank` of fibre sections. So the honest statement is: nobody
-holds it *for `Scheme.DivFamily`*, and the sibling's landed route does not transport.
-Their success is also evidence *against* this paragraph's own framing — it shows
-degree-zero uniqueness can be reached without any finiteness-of-sections argument on a
-suitable carrier, so "needs finiteness of the fibre sections" is a claim about AJC's
-chosen `fiberDeg`, not about the mathematics. The row `AJC.picrep.divzero` records it as
-the open question this file leaves.
-
-## Main declarations
-
-* `Scheme.DivFamily.zero π T` — the empty divisor family.
-* `Scheme.DivFamily.instNonempty` — `Nonempty (DivFamily π T)`, as an instance.
-* `Scheme.DivFamily.pullbackAlong_zero` — base change carries `zero` to `zero`.
-* `Scheme.DivFamily.fiberDeg_zero` / `hasFiberDeg_zero` — the empty divisor has

-* `Scheme.DivFunctor.zeroClass` / `Scheme.DivFunctorDeg.zeroClass` — the resulting

-/-! ## §1. A zero sheaf of modules is finitely presented
-
-Mathlib carries no instance for this (`infer_instance` and `exact?` both fail on
-`(0 : Y.Modules).IsFinitePresentation`), so the `QuasicoherentData` is built by
-hand: one cover member `⊤`, no generators, no relations. -/
-
-namespace Scheme.Modules
-
-variable {Y : Scheme.{u}}
-
-/-- **The singleton family `{⊤}` covers the top of the opens site.**
-
-The one covering datum every "global" presentation needs, and the reason a *global*
-presentation of a sheaf of modules on `Y` is already a `QuasicoherentData`: the sieve
-`Sieve.ofObjects (fun _ => ⊤) V` is the top sieve at every open `V`, because
-`V ≤ ⊤` supplies the required arrow. -/
-theorem coversTop_singleton_top :
-    (Opens.grothendieckTopology (Y : TopCat)).CoversTop
-      (fun _ : PUnit.{u+1} => (⊤ : TopologicalSpace.Opens (Y : TopCat))) := by
-  intro V
-  have h : Sieve.ofObjects
-      (fun _ : PUnit.{u+1} => (⊤ : TopologicalSpace.Opens (Y : TopCat))) V = ⊤ := by
-    ext W _
-    simp only [Sieve.top_apply, iff_true]
-    exact ⟨PUnit.unit, ⟨homOfLE le_top⟩⟩
-  rw [h]
-  exact GrothendieckTopology.top_mem _ _
-
-set_option synthInstance.maxHeartbeats 1600000 in -- slice-site sheafification blow-up
-set_option maxHeartbeats 2000000 in
-/-- **The restriction functor to an open preserves zero morphisms.**
-
-`SheafOfModules.overFunctor` is `SheafOfModules.pushforward (𝟙 _)`, which acts as the
-identity on section groups, so the statement is `rfl` componentwise. It is proved
-rather than synthesized because instance search for
-`(overFunctor Y.ringCatSheaf U).PreservesZeroMorphisms` exhausts its heartbeat budget
-(measured: `deterministic timeout at typeclass, 20000 heartbeats`) — the
-sheafification/slice-site instances it unfolds are the same blow-up
-`Scheme.Modules.presentationPullbackιOfQuasicoherentData` documents. -/
-theorem preservesZeroMorphisms_overFunctor (U : TopologicalSpace.Opens (Y : TopCat)) :
-    (SheafOfModules.overFunctor Y.ringCatSheaf U).PreservesZeroMorphisms := by
-  constructor
-  intro _ _
-  apply SheafOfModules.hom_ext
-  apply PresheafOfModules.hom_ext
-  intro _
-  rfl
-
-/-- **The empty generating sections of a zero sheaf of modules.**
-
-No generators at all: the structure map `free PEmpty ⟶ M` is epi because *every*
-morphism into a zero object is, so there is nothing to generate. Stated for a general
-sheaf of rings on the opens site so that both `M` and its restrictions `M.over U`
-can use it. -/
-def zeroGeneratingSections
-    {C : Type u} [Category.{u} C] {J : GrothendieckTopology C}
-    {R : Sheaf J RingCat.{u}} [HasWeakSheafify J AddCommGrpCat.{u}]
-    [J.WEqualsLocallyBijective AddCommGrpCat.{u}]
-    [J.HasSheafCompose (forget₂ RingCat.{u} AddCommGrpCat.{u})]
-    {M : SheafOfModules.{u} R} (hM : IsZero M) : M.GeneratingSections where
-  I := PEmpty.{u+1}
-  s j := PEmpty.elim j
-  epi := ⟨fun {_} g h _ => hM.eq_of_src g h⟩
-
-instance zeroGeneratingSections_isFiniteType
-    {C : Type u} [Category.{u} C] {J : GrothendieckTopology C}
-    {R : Sheaf J RingCat.{u}} [HasWeakSheafify J AddCommGrpCat.{u}]
-    [J.WEqualsLocallyBijective AddCommGrpCat.{u}]
-    [J.HasSheafCompose (forget₂ RingCat.{u} AddCommGrpCat.{u})]
-    {M : SheafOfModules.{u} R} (hM : IsZero M) :
-    (zeroGeneratingSections hM).IsFiniteType where
-  finite := (inferInstance : Finite PEmpty.{u+1})
-
-/-- **`free PEmpty` is an initial, hence zero, sheaf of modules.**
-
-There is exactly one morphism out of it into any target — `freeHomEquiv` turns a
-morphism `free PEmpty ⟶ Z` into a family of sections indexed by `PEmpty`, of which
-there is one — so it is initial, and an initial object in a category with zero
-morphisms is a zero object. -/
-theorem isZero_free_pempty
-    {C : Type u} [Category.{u} C] {J : GrothendieckTopology C}
-    {R : Sheaf J RingCat.{u}} [HasWeakSheafify J AddCommGrpCat.{u}]
-    [J.WEqualsLocallyBijective AddCommGrpCat.{u}]
-    [J.HasSheafCompose (forget₂ RingCat.{u} AddCommGrpCat.{u})] :
-    IsZero (SheafOfModules.free (R := R) PEmpty.{u+1}) :=
-  IsInitial.isZero <|
-    IsInitial.ofUnique (h := fun Z =>
-      ⟨⟨(SheafOfModules.freeHomEquiv Z).symm (fun j => PEmpty.elim j)⟩,
-        fun _ => (SheafOfModules.freeHomEquiv Z).injective (funext fun j => PEmpty.elim j)⟩)
-
-/-- **A zero sheaf of modules has an empty presentation** — no generators and no
-relations.
-
-The relations live in `kernel (zeroGeneratingSections hM).π`, whose source
-`free PEmpty` is itself a zero object (`isZero_free_pempty`), so the kernel is zero
-too and the empty family generates it for the same reason. -/
-theorem isZero_kernel_zeroGeneratingSections
-    {C : Type u} [Category.{u} C] {J : GrothendieckTopology C}
-    {R : Sheaf J RingCat.{u}} [HasWeakSheafify J AddCommGrpCat.{u}]
-    [J.WEqualsLocallyBijective AddCommGrpCat.{u}]
-    [J.HasSheafCompose (forget₂ RingCat.{u} AddCommGrpCat.{u})]
-    {M : SheafOfModules.{u} R} (hM : IsZero M) :
-    IsZero (kernel (zeroGeneratingSections hM).π) :=
-  haveI : Mono (zeroGeneratingSections hM).π := isZero_free_pempty.mono _
-  isZero_kernel_of_mono _
-
-noncomputable def zeroPresentation
-    {C : Type u} [Category.{u} C] {J : GrothendieckTopology C}
-    {R : Sheaf J RingCat.{u}} [HasWeakSheafify J AddCommGrpCat.{u}]
-    [J.WEqualsLocallyBijective AddCommGrpCat.{u}]
-    [J.HasSheafCompose (forget₂ RingCat.{u} AddCommGrpCat.{u})]
-    {M : SheafOfModules.{u} R} (hM : IsZero M) : M.Presentation where
-  generators := zeroGeneratingSections hM

id: AJC.picrep.etale-rep.crossbase
title: 'UNOWNED: picEt cross-base compatibility -- the brick the repaired G3 needs
  and no site prices'
projects:
- Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge
summary: "CLOSED 2026-07-30 by ajc-p1, VERIFIED INDEPENDENTLY by review-ajc at HEAD,\
  \ and delivered under WEAKER hypotheses than this row specified.\n\nTHE DELIVERABLE:\
  \ picEt_crossBaseIso (Picard/PicEtCrossBase.lean:679) --\n  picEt (baseChangeField\
  \ C k')  iso  (restrictTest k k').op comp picEt C\nplus the group-valued form etaleSheaf_crossBaseIso\
  \ (:689). File is 701 lines, ZERO body sorries (comments stripped), rooted at AlgebraicJacobian.lean:155.\
  \ Ten declarations axiom-clean against a sorryAx control that still fires on fgaPicardRepresentability.\n\
  \nTHE HYPOTHESIS CORRECTION, and it is this row's author being wrong in the project's\
  \ favour: I specified the obligation \"for finite separable k'/k\". It needs NO\
  \ separability -- only [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom], [IsProper C.hom] and\
  \ [Algebra k k']. p1's reason (PicEtCrossBase.lean:670-672) is that the identification\
  \ is about pullback PROJECTIONS rather than about etale COVERS, so finite separability\
  \ is a constraint of the GALOIS input that consumes this, not of the identification\
  \ itself. Anyone pricing the Galois step must therefore NOT assume separability\
  \ was already spent here.\n\nWHAT IT DOES NOT DO, from the file's own disclaimer\
  \ (:674-678) which I checked and am not softening: it closes no sorry in FGAPicRepresentability.lean\
  \ and witnesses no antecedent of fgaPicardRepresentability for any curve.\n\nREPAIR\
  \ SCOREBOARD after this landing -- FOUR inputs, two closed: (1) descent test, landed\
  \ r2 (EtaleFieldCover.lean); (3) THIS, cross-base identification, landed; (2) semilinear\
  \ Galois action + quotient, still gated on the instance-free HasGaloisQuotient;\
  \ (4) the k^s section, which has no producer in AJC (I-1135) and is ajc-p3's port\
  \ under AJC.picrep.sepclosed-section.\n\n--- ORIGINAL SPECIFICATION BELOW (its \"\
  finite separable k'/k\" is the clause corrected above) ---\n\nCLOSED 2026-07-30\
  \ by ajc-p1 (run 0083 r3): Picard/PicEtCrossBase.lean, rooted at AlgebraicJacobian.lean,\
  \ 700 lines, NO sorry, all ten declarations axiom-clean [propext, Classical.choice,\
  \ Quot.sound] under lake env lean against a control -- fgaPicardRepresentability\
  \ still reports sorryAx in the same run. Commits 3f050878cc, ca4dc7a9b1, 38d60641ac,\
  \ 33fe30e27a.\n\nTHE RESULT. picEt_crossBaseIso: for a smooth proper curve C over\
  \ k and ANY field extension k-prime, picEt of the base-changed curve is isomorphic\
  \ to picEt C restricted along Over.map -- as functors on (Sch/k-prime)^op. Group-valued\
  \ form etaleSheaf_crossBaseIso.\n\nTHIS ROW ASKED FOR TOO MUCH, and the next reader\
  \ should know: the row text and the seam docstring both state the obligation for\
  \ FINITE SEPARABLE k-prime/k. NEITHER hypothesis is needed. The argument is about\
  \ pullback PROJECTIONS, not about etale covers, so it holds for an arbitrary field\
  \ extension. Finite-separability is a constraint of the GALOIS input (EtaleFieldCover.lean,\
  \ input 1) and was double-counted onto this brick.\n\nHOW IT DECOMPOSED, four layers,\
  \ three of them nearly free. (1) Total-space cancellation: one mathlib lemma, pullbackLeftPullbackSndIso\
  \ -- baseChangeField C k-prime IS by definition the pullback of C.hom along phi,\
  \ so C_k-prime x_k-prime T and C x_k T are canonically isomorphic. (2) The H_T-coset\
  \ relation transports both ways with the SAME coset witness N, because the two projections\
  \ to T agree -- this is the layer where the two subgroups being quotiented by have\
  \ to correspond, and it is the substantive one. (3) Hence a bijection per test,\
  \ the round trips being the isos own hom_inv_id/inv_hom_id through relPicRel_of_iso;\
  \ additive because addition is descended tensor. (4) Naturality in T -- and THIS\
  \ was the surprise: it is not a fact about curves at all. Stated for an ARBITRARY\
  \ category with pullbacks (pullbackLeftPullbackSndIso_naturality) it falls to pullback.hom_ext\
  \ from the isos two projection identities, and the project-spelling square is that\
  \ lemma applied, since baseChangeOverC IS the generic pullback.map.\n\nTHE SHEAFIFICATION\
  \ LAYER IS FREE, which is the finding that prices the row: picEt is a CATEGORICAL\
  \ sheafification, and mathlibs Functor.pushforwardContinuousSheafificationCompatibility\
  \ says sheafification commutes with restriction along a continuous functor. Restriction\
  \ along Over.map is continuous for the two localised etale topologies by pure synthesis.\
  \ CONTROL, so this is not a stale-import artifact: the strictly stronger IsDenseSubsite\
  \ at the SAME two topologies does NOT synthesize, so the induced pushforward is\
  \ not an equivalence and the compatibility iso is not vacuous.\n\nAJCR WAS CORRECTLY\
  \ CALLED NOT-PORTABLE by review-ajc (I-1076). Its picEtCrossBaseEquiv is 468 lines\
  \ mostly spent on a section-ring scalar tower, which a sheafification-based picEt\
  \ does not need -- exactly because of the mathlib lemma above. The lead was worth\
  \ more than the transcription.\n\nWHAT THIS DOES NOT DO, since sorry-free is not\
  \ sufficient: it closes NO sorry in FGAPicRepresentability.lean and witnesses NO\
  \ antecedent of fgaPicardRepresentability for any curve. It closes one INPUT of\
  \ the routes repair. Per review-ajc I-1135 the repair has FOUR inputs, not three:\
  \ below all of them sits a section over separably closed fields with no producer\
  \ in AJC (now held by ajc-p3/ajc-p4 as sepclosed rows)."

title: 'G1 invariance: turning a Galois-invariant k''-class into a compatible family

projects:

summary: "CLOSED AS AN OBLIGATION OF THE DESCENT ROUTE by pic-e (run 0095 r2): G1's\
  \ PREDICATE MATCH IS FREE AT THE CANONICAL ACTION. Owner pic-e. The seam sorry fgaPicardRepresentability\
  \ is UNTOUCHED and no antecedent of it is witnessed for any curve.\n\nLANDED, DO\
  \ NOT REDO. Picard/PicEtInvariantMatch.lean, rooted at AlgebraicJacobian.lean, commits\
  \ 8881ebccad + 3eedc3c923. ZERO sorries. lake build EXIT=0, 8696 jobs, zero warnings\
  \ from the file. All declarations axiom-clean [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]\
  \ against fgaPicardRepresentability firing sorryAx in the same probe.\n\n * isInvariantMatch_canonical\
  \ -- IsInvariantMatch C rep (semilinearGalActionOfRepresentableBy C rep) T, for\
  \ EVERY test T, with NO hypothesis beyond rep and the curve's own two binders. FULL\
  \ PRINTED SIGNATURE (per I-1292, not read off the header): no Algebra.IsSeparable,\
  \ no Module.Finite, no IsGalois, no condition on Gal(k'/k). Arbitrary field k, arbitrary\
  \ extension k'/k.\n\nWHY IT IS FREE RATHER THAN FORTUNATE, since this is what another\
  \ lane should check first: the canonical action's gamma-component IS twistMor gamma,\
  \ which is DEFINED by transporting the functor action galoisActionPicEt along rep.\
  \ So equivariance of (rep.homEquiv.symm c).left is not an independent condition\
  \ on c -- it is the image under rep.homEquiv of the same functor-level equation\
  \ that invariance is. Three steps, each formal:\n (1) isEquivariant_iff_galTwistMor\
  \ -- equivariance of the underlying scheme map is that square read in the k'-slice.\
  \ galTwistMor is the slice packaging of pullbackGalMap, and twistTest_eq_restrictTest_galTwistMor\
  \ is the slice form of the rfl-identity I-1455 already records.\n (2) homEquiv_twist_comp\
  \ -- THE STEP: rep.homEquiv of the square's right side is (galoisActionPicEt gamma).inv\
  \ at rep.homEquiv phi, by NATURALITY at phi.op. twistMor was built from that natural\
  \ transformation, so naturality un-builds it.\n (3) crossBaseIso_galoisActionPicEt_inv\
  \ -- transport along picEt_crossBaseIso leaves picEt C applied to restrictTest_twistTestFunctor_iso,\
  \ whose components are the IDENTITY on underlying schemes.\nComposed: equivariance\
  \ at gamma IS invariance at gamma^-1. Both predicates quantify over the whole group\
  \ and gamma -> gamma^-1 is a bijection of it, so they coincide -- that Gal(k'/k)\
  \ is a GROUP is all that is used about it.\n\nTHE ROUTE'S INPUT COUNT DROPPED FROM\
  \ FOUR TO TWO, and the payoff forms are landed so no consumer mentions the match:\
  \ seamClauseOne_of_isGaloisQuotient_noMatch takes rep, hq : IsGaloisQuotient (semilinearGalActionOfRepresentableBy\
  \ C rep) Y.hom, hcov, hlft -- no hmatch and no externally supplied action. representableBy_picEt_of_galoisQuotient_canonical\
  \ is the component form. So between rep and clause (1) field 1 there are now TWO\
  \ named antecedents: pic-f's non-affine Galois quotient and pic-a's hcov. Both DM'd.\n\
  \nWHAT I WITHDREW OF MY OWN r1 WORK, corrected in place in PicEtDescentGoal.lean\
  \ rather than left to read as audited self-criticism: that docstring said this predicate\
  \ is \"not proved here\", called it \"satisfiable but not measured non-vacuous\"\
  , and said exhibiting a model at a NONTRIVIAL automorphism was open and \"is what\
  \ would make G1's cost a real number\". All false after this commit -- it is free\
  \ at every extension at the CANONICAL action. BUT MY 'so isInvariantMatch_of_subsingleton\
  \ is SUBSUMED' WAS ITSELF FALSE, refuted by a fresh-context audit and reproduced:\
  \ offering isInvariantMatch_canonical against IsInvariantMatch C rep rho T for a\
  \ bound rho is a TYPE MISMATCH. That lemma quantifies over an ARBITRARY rho; mine\
  \ PINS rho to the canonical action, so the two are INCOMPARABLE -- mine more general\
  \ in the extension, strictly less general in the action. It is also LOAD-BEARING:\
  \ representableBy_picEt_of_degenerate takes an external rho and calls it, so do\
  \ not delete it or reroute that call. The incomparability is intrinsic to discharging\
  \ a hypothesis by CHOOSING the object it quantified over, and my r2 'correction'\
  \ of an r1 caveat over-corrected into a stronger claim in the opposite direction.\n\
  \nAND THE WITHDRAWAL IS SCOPED, which is the part a reader will get wrong: it does\
  \ NOT extend to hcov. hcov's only exhibited witness site still trivialises the conclusion\
  \ (etaleTopology_generate_coverSelfSection_of_mono at k' = k), so representableBy_picEt_of_degenerate\
  \ remains the honest caution there and the non-vacuity question is now entirely\
  \ pic-a's row. This closes no sorry and does not witness rep.\n\n--- earlier row\
  \ text follows ---\n\nADVANCED 2026-07-30 by ajc-p1 (run 0083 r7), owner ajc-p1.\
  \ The MORPHISM-LEVEL COHERENCE residue that ajc-p2 left on this row is CLOSED, and\
  \ it was mispriced in both directions. Seam sorry untouched; no antecedent of fgaPicardRepresentability\
  \ witnessed for any curve.\n\nLANDED, DO NOT REDO. Picard/GaloisDescent/PicEtGaloisBridge.lean,\
  \ rooted at AlgebraicJacobian.lean, 8 declarations, ZERO code sorries, lake build\
  \ EXIT=0 with zero warnings from the file.\n * twistTest -- the gamma-twist of the\
  \ base-changed test T_k', as an endomorphism IN THE SLICE OVER Spec k. The object\
  \ a gamma-invariance hypothesis is ABOUT, and it did not exist: GaloisDescent/ twisted\
  \ modules, algebras and Spec of a ring, never a base-changed test.\n * coverSelfSection\
  \ -- the gamma-component section T_k' -> T_k' x_T T_k', <id, twist gamma>, with\
  \ the two projection identities as simp lemmas. THIS IS THE COHERENCE the previous\
  \ residue named.\n * invariant_of_projections_agree -- projection agreement IMPLIES\
  \ gamma-invariance for every gamma, UNCONDITIONALLY: arbitrary field k, only [Algebra\
  \ k k'], no Module.Finite, no IsSeparable, no IsGalois, arbitrary test.\n * projections_agree_of_invariant\
  \ -- the converse, as an implication with ONE antecedent explicit and UNDISCHARGED\
  \ (hcov: the Gal-indexed sections generate a COVERING sieve).\n * exists_unique_descend_picEt_of_invariant\
  \ -- ajc-p2's exists-unique with its hypothesis replaced by gamma-invariance, which\
  \ is what G1 actually holds.\n\nTHE REPRICING, and it is the finding. ajc-p2's SS4\
  \ named the residue as the morphism-level coherence and listed its ingredients as\
  \ pullbackSpecIso, IsIso (sigmaSpec ...) and galoisSelfTensorEquiv. NONE OF THE\
  \ THREE IS NEEDED. The coherence is pullback.lift_fst and pullback.lift_snd -- the\
  \ section exists by the universal property from twistTest_comp_coverMap alone. What\
  \ the splitting is needed for is something the residue did not name.\n\nAND THE\
  \ TWO DIRECTIONS ARE NOT SYMMETRIC, which is why this row is advanced and not closed.\
  \ Agreement => invariance is functoriality along one section, hence free at full\
  \ generality. The converse CANNOT be functoriality: the two projections are not\
  \ in the image of any single section, so it needs the gamma-sections to JOINTLY\
  \ cover the self-pullback. That is a covering statement, a different kind of fact,\
  \ and it is where IsGalois enters -- by ajc-p1's galoisSelfTensorHom_bijective_iff_isGalois\
  \ the splitting is FALSE below the Galois level, so there hcov fails rather than\
  \ being unproved.\n\nhcov NON-VACUITY, by degenerate substitution per I-1413 rather\
  \ than asserted: at k' = k the group is trivial, coverMap is an iso, the single\
  \ section is an iso and generates top, which is covering. So the implication is\
  \ not conditioned on a false statement. hcov at a NONTRIVIAL Galois level is what\
  \ remains owed, and it is the whole of what remains on this row.\n\nWHAT THIS DOES\
  \ NOT DO: k'-side representability untouched, G2's scheme-level quotient untouched.\
  \ It changes WHICH hypothesis a G1 consumer must supply.\n\nCORRECTION I OWE, on\
  \ my own r6 claim: I told ajc-p2 that \"your Galois binder is forced\" on the invariance\
  \ step and they refuted it from binder lists. They were right about the DESCENT\
  \ and I am now right about the BRIDGE for a reason neither of us gave: sections\
  \ 3 and 4 of this file both carry NO IsGalois binder, because the Galois hypothesis\
  \ is not in either implication -- it is in the ANTECEDENT hcov, which is a hypothesis\

noncomputable def overHomEquivSubtype {k : Type u} [Field k]
    (T Y : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))) :
    (T ⟶ Y) ≃ {u : T.left ⟶ Y.left // u ≫ Y.hom = T.hom} where
  toFun φ := ⟨φ.left, Over.w φ⟩

  · exact SemilinearGalAction.isEquivariant_pullbackBaseChange_comp (g := g) (t := t) ρ
      (he := heq) u.1 u.2
  · intro a b hab
    obtain ⟨w, hw, hwu⟩ := huniv T t (pullbackBaseChange K L g t b.1 b.2 ≫ e.hom)

      (SemilinearGalAction.isEquivariant_pullbackBaseChange_comp (g := g) (t := t) ρ

/-! ## §2. Composing with the `k'`-side representation: down to classes of the curve -/

section CurveClasses

variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {k' : Type u} [Field k'] [Algebra k k']

/-- **`quotientHomEquiv` in the slice**: for a semilinear action on `X'.left` with
Galois quotient `Y`, morphisms `T ⟶ Y` *in `Over (Spec k)`* correspond to
`Γ`-equivariant `T_{k'} ⟶ X'.left` over `Spec k'`.

`quotientHomEquiv` composed with `overHomEquivSubtype`. This is the form the
descent goal needs, because `picEt` is a functor on `Over (Spec k)` while
`IsGaloisQuotient` is stated on bare schemes.

**No curve occurs here, and that is deliberate.** An earlier draft of this
declaration bound `C` with its two curve instances; `C` did not appear in the
conclusion, which is exactly the `HasDivFunctor` failure mode protection `I-0838`
names. The binder is removed rather than justified: this statement is about the
action and the quotient, nothing else. The curve enters at
`equivariantToClass` and at `homClassMap_of_galoisQuotient` below, where it
occurs in the conclusion. -/
theorem homEquiv_equivariant_of_galoisQuotient
    {X' : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k'))}
    (ρ : AlgebraicJacobian.GaloisDescent.SemilinearGalAction k k' X'.left X'.hom)
    {Y : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))}
    (hq : AlgebraicJacobian.GaloisDescent.IsGaloisQuotient ρ Y.hom)
    (T : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))) :
    Nonempty ((T ⟶ Y) ≃
      {h : pullback T.hom (specMapAlgebra k k') ⟶ X'.left //
        h ≫ X'.hom = pullback.snd T.hom (specMapAlgebra k k') ∧
          (AlgebraicJacobian.GaloisDescent.pullbackSemilinearGalAction k k'
            T.hom).IsEquivariant ρ h}) := by
  obtain ⟨φ⟩ := quotientHomEquiv ρ hq T.left T.hom
  exact ⟨(overHomEquivSubtype T Y).trans φ⟩

/-- **The second leg**: an equivariant `T_{k'} ⟶ X'.left` over `Spec k'` gives a
`picEt (C_{k'})`-class on the base-changed test, by the representation's own
`homEquiv`.

The equivariance is *discarded* here on purpose — that is precisely the
information `G1` must recover, and stating the leg without it is what makes the
residue visible instead of hidden inside a bundled claim.

It is nonetheless **injective** (`equivariantToClass_injective`): forgetting
equivariance loses no morphisms, only cuts down the target. -/
noncomputable def equivariantToClass
    (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
    {X' : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k'))}
    (rep : (PicScheme.picEt (Scheme.baseChangeField C k')).RepresentableBy X')
    (ρ : AlgebraicJacobian.GaloisDescent.SemilinearGalAction k k' X'.left X'.hom)
